title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
shortDescription: Spaghetti, garlic, olive oil, chili flake, parsley
note: Save a mugful of starchy pasta water before draining — it's what makes the sauce cling instead of pooling.
introCopy: The whole dish is really just garlic bloomed slowly in good olive oil until it turns sweet, not sharp. Four ingredients, but the timing matters more than usual.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti until just shy of al dente.
While pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a wide skillet over low heat. Add garlic and chili flake.
Cook garlic slowly, stirring often, until pale gold and fragrant — don't let it brown or it turns bitter.
Transfer pasta directly into the skillet with tongs, along with a splash of pasta water.
Toss vigorously over heat, adding pasta water as needed, until the sauce looks glossy and coats the noodles.
Off heat, stir in parsley, taste for salt, and serve immediately.

title: Baked Ziti
shortDescription: Ziti, ricotta, marinara, mozzarella, basil
note: Undercook the pasta by two minutes — it finishes in the oven and you want it to still have bite.
introCopy: The kind of dish you make on a Sunday for a week of Tuesdays. Freezes well before or after baking.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400°F. Boil ziti two minutes short of package directions.
Stir ricotta, egg, half the parmesan, and a pinch of salt together in a bowl.
Toss drained pasta with marinara and the ricotta mixture until evenly coated.
Spread half into a baking dish, scatter half the mozzarella, then repeat with the rest.
Top with remaining parmesan and bake uncovered until bubbling and golden at the edges.
Rest five minutes, scatter with basil, and serve.

title: Chicken Piccata
shortDescription: Chicken breast, capers, lemon, butter, cornstarch dredge
note: Pound the chicken to an even thickness first — that's what keeps it from drying out before the sauce reduces.
introCopy: Bright, salty, and quick — a good one for when you want a restaurant dish on a weeknight clock.

steps.text: Season cutlets and dredge lightly in cornstarch, shaking off excess.
Brown cutlets in 2 tbsp butter over medium-high heat, 3 minutes per side. Set aside.
Add stock, lemon juice, and capers to the pan, scraping up the browned bits.
Simmer until reduced by a third, then swirl in remaining butter.
Return chicken to the pan to warm through and coat in sauce before serving.

imageCredit: Infrogmation of New Orleans / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Black Bean Tacos
shortDescription: Black beans, corn tortillas, avocado, lime, cabbage
note: Smash a portion of the beans against the pan — it thickens the filling so it doesn't fall out of the tortilla.
introCopy: Pantry tacos that don't taste like a compromise. Good with whatever hot sauce you already have open.

steps.text: Warm beans with cumin and a splash of water in a skillet, mashing about half of them.
Char tortillas directly over a burner flame or in a dry skillet.
Fill tortillas with bean mash, cabbage, and avocado.
Squeeze lime over the top and serve with hot sauce.

title: Chicken Tinga Tacos
shortDescription: Shredded chicken, chipotle, tomato, onion, corn tortillas
note: Poach the chicken in the same broth you'll use for the sauce base — no flavor left behind.
introCopy: Smoky, a little sweet from the chipotle, and endlessly reheatable — this one gets better on day two.

steps.text: Simmer chicken thighs in salted water with half the onion until cooked through, then shred.
Blend tomatoes, chipotles, garlic, and remaining onion into a smooth sauce.
Simmer the sauce in a skillet until it deepens in color and thickens slightly.
Fold shredded chicken into the sauce and warm through.
Serve in warmed tortillas with your usual taco toppings.

imageCredit: Infrogmation of New Orleans / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

title: Carne Asada
shortDescription: Skirt steak, lime, garlic, cilantro, orange
note: Slice against the grain — with skirt steak this matters more than almost anything else you do to it.
introCopy: A weekend grill dish. Marinate in the morning, cook it fast and hot in the evening.

steps.text: Whisk citrus juices, garlic, cilantro, and olive oil together for the marinade.
Marinate steak at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Grill or sear over very high heat, about 3 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice thin against the grain.

title: Miso-Glazed Salmon
shortDescription: Salmon, white miso, mirin, ginger, scallion
note: Broil close to the top rack for the last two minutes to get real char on the glaze — don't walk away.
introCopy: A four-ingredient glaze that does a lot of work. Good over rice, good over greens, good cold the next day.

steps.text: Whisk miso, mirin, tamari, and ginger into a glaze.
Coat salmon in the glaze and let sit 10 minutes at room temperature.
Bake at 400°F until nearly cooked through.
Switch to broil for the final 2 minutes to char the glaze.
Scatter with scallions and serve.

imageCredit: Liat Portal for Foodie Disorder / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Vegetable Yaki Udon
shortDescription: Udon noodles, cabbage, carrot, mushroom, tamari
note: Fresh or vacuum-packed udon works far better here than dried — dried needs a separate boil first.
introCopy: A stir-fry that comes together in one pan once the vegetables are cut. Good vehicle for whatever's wilting in the crisper.

steps.text: Loosen udon noodles under warm water to separate the strands.
Stir-fry carrot and mushroom in oil over high heat until just tender.
Add cabbage and cook until it wilts but keeps some bite.
Add noodles and tamari, tossing until everything is glossy and heated through.

title: Chicken Katsu
shortDescription: Chicken thigh, panko, katsu sauce, cabbage
note: Rest the breaded cutlets for five minutes before frying — it helps the crust stay put in the oil.
introCopy: The crunch is the whole point. Double-dredge if you want it extra thick.

steps.text: Dredge chicken in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing to adhere.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 340°F until deeply golden, about 4 minutes per side.
Drain on a rack, then slice into strips.
Serve over shredded cabbage with katsu sauce.

imageCredit: Alpha from Melbourne, Australia / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Chana Masala
shortDescription: Chickpeas, tomato, onion, garam masala, ginger
note: Bloom the garam masala in the oil for thirty seconds before adding liquid — dry spices need fat and heat to open up.
introCopy: A pantry curry that scales up without any trouble. Better the day after it's made.

steps.text: Sauté onion in oil until deeply golden, not just soft.
Add ginger-garlic paste and dry spices, stirring until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer until the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Add chickpeas and a splash of water, then simmer to thicken.
Serve hot over steamed basmati rice.

title: Butter Chicken
shortDescription: Chicken thigh, tomato, cream, butter, garam masala
note: Marinate the chicken in yogurt overnight if you have time — it tenderizes as much as it flavors.
introCopy: Rich and a little sweet from the cream. Worth the extra ten minutes of simmering for the sauce to deepen.

steps.text: Marinate chicken in yogurt and half the garam masala at least 30 minutes.
Sear chicken in a hot pan until browned, then set aside.
Melt butter in the same pan and add tomato puree and remaining spices.
Simmer sauce until it deepens in color, about 15 minutes.
Stir in cream and return chicken to the pan to finish cooking through.
Serve over steamed basmati rice.

title: Saag Paneer
shortDescription: Spinach, paneer, garlic, ginger, cream
note: Blanch the spinach briefly before blending — it keeps the color bright instead of turning drab olive.
introCopy: Iron-rich and creamy without being heavy. Paneer holds its shape well, so don't overcook it once it's in the sauce.

steps.text: Blanch spinach 1 minute, then blend into a rough puree.
Sauté onion, ginger, and garlic until soft.
Add spinach puree and garam masala, simmering 5 minutes.
Fold in paneer and cream, warming through without a hard boil.
Serve over steamed basmati rice.

title: Vegetable Green Curry
shortDescription: Green curry paste, coconut milk, eggplant, bell pepper, basil
note: Fry the curry paste in the thick coconut cream that rises to the top of the can — it blooms the flavor far more than adding it to thin liquid.
introCopy: As fast as takeout once the vegetables are chopped, and you control how much heat goes in.

ingredients.prepNote: check for shrimp paste if strict vegan

steps.text: Scoop the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk can and fry with curry paste until fragrant.
Add remaining coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add eggplant and simmer until nearly tender.
Add bell pepper and tamari, cooking until the pepper is just tender.
Stir in basil off heat and serve over rice.

title: Pad See Ew with Chicken
shortDescription: Wide rice noodles, chicken, chinese broccoli, dark soy
note: Get the pan smoking hot before the noodles go in — that's where the char flavor comes from, not from the sauce.
introCopy: A high-heat, fast-moving stir-fry. Have every ingredient measured out before the pan goes on.

steps.text: Sear chicken in a very hot wok until just cooked, then push to one side.
Crack eggs into the empty side and scramble briefly.
Add noodles, broccoli, dark soy, and oyster sauce, tossing constantly.
Cook until noodles pick up some char and broccoli is tender-crisp.

imageCredit: Ser Amantio di Nicolao / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Tom Yum Goong
shortDescription: Shrimp, lemongrass, lime leaf, mushroom, chili
note: Bruise the lemongrass and lime leaves instead of chopping them fine — you want the aromatics infused, not eaten.
introCopy: Sour, hot, and fast. The broth should taste sharp enough to make your eyes water a little.

steps.text: Simmer shrimp shells in water 10 minutes to build a quick stock, then strain.
Add lemongrass, lime leaves, and mushrooms to the stock and simmer.
Add shrimp and cook just until pink and opaque.
Off heat, stir in fish sauce and lime juice to taste.

title: Baked Falafel Bowl
shortDescription: Chickpeas, parsley, cumin, tahini, cucumber
note: Don't skip the resting time for the batter — dry chickpea flour needs it to bind, or the falafel fall apart in the oven.
introCopy: Baked instead of fried, which trades a little crunch for a lot less cleanup.

steps.text: Pulse soaked (uncooked) chickpeas, parsley, and cumin in a food processor to a coarse paste.
Rest the mixture in the fridge to firm up.
Form into balls, brush with oil, and bake at 400°F, turning once.
Assemble bowls with rice or greens, cucumber, falafel, and tahini sauce.

title: Shakshuka
shortDescription: Eggs poached in tomato, bell pepper, cumin, feta
note: Crack the eggs into small cups first before sliding them in — it keeps the yolks intact and evenly spaced.
introCopy: Breakfast, lunch, or dinner, eaten straight from the pan with something to mop up the sauce.

steps.text: Sauté onion and pepper until soft.
Add crushed tomatoes and cumin, simmering until thickened.
Make wells in the sauce and slide in the eggs.
Cover and cook until whites are set but yolks are still soft.
Scatter feta over the top and serve straight from the pan.

title: Lamb Kofta
shortDescription: Ground lamb, cumin, cinnamon, onion, parsley
note: Wet your hands before shaping the kofta — the mixture is sticky and this keeps it from clumping to your fingers.
introCopy: Skewered and grilled, spiced with a warmth that leans more toward cinnamon than heat.

steps.text: Mix lamb, onion, parsley, and spices thoroughly by hand.
Shape into logs around skewers, chilling 15 minutes if the mixture feels soft.
Grill or sear over high heat, turning to brown all sides.
Rest a few minutes before serving.

title: Turkey Chili
shortDescription: Ground turkey, kidney beans, tomato, chili powder, bell pepper
note: Let it simmer uncovered for the last stretch — that's what thickens it instead of leaving it soupy.
introCopy: A weeknight staple that's easy to double for the freezer. Leaner than beef chili but doesn't skimp on flavor if the spices are generous.

steps.text: Brown turkey with onion and bell pepper, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in chili powder and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and beans, bringing to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until thickened.

title: Sheet-Pan Salmon and Asparagus
shortDescription: Salmon, asparagus, lemon, olive oil, dill
note: Add the asparagus to the pan a few minutes after the salmon starts — it cooks faster and turns to mush if it goes in at the same time.
introCopy: One pan, minimal cleanup, and on the table in under thirty minutes.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425°F. Place salmon on a sheet pan, drizzle with oil, season.
Roast salmon alone for 4 minutes.
Add asparagus and lemon slices to the pan and continue roasting.
Scatter with dill and serve.

title: Classic Smash Burger
shortDescription: Ground beef, American cheese, brioche bun, pickles
note: Smash the patty within seconds of it hitting the pan — waiting even a minute means it won't get the crust.
introCopy: Thin, crispy-edged patties beat a thick one for flavor almost every time. Two per bun if you're hungry.

steps.text: Divide beef into loose balls, season, and place on a screaming hot griddle.
Smash flat immediately with a spatula and let sear undisturbed.
Flip, add cheese, and cook until melted.
Build burgers on toasted buns with onion and pickles.

title: Mapo Tofu
shortDescription: Silken tofu, doubanjiang, sichuan peppercorn, scallion
note: Slide the tofu in gently and stop stirring hard once it's added — silken tofu breaks apart if you're rough with it.
introCopy: Numbing, savory, and fast once the sauce base is built. The vegetable version below skips the usual ground pork.

steps.text: Fry doubanjiang in oil until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add stock and bring to a simmer.
Gently slide in tofu cubes and simmer 5 minutes without stirring hard.
Stir in cornstarch slurry to thicken slightly.
Top with scallions and ground Sichuan peppercorn.
Serve hot over steamed white rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
shortDescription: Chicken, peanuts, dried chili, scallion, sichuan peppercorn
note: Marinate the chicken in a little cornstarch and soy — it's the classic velveting trick that keeps stir-fried chicken tender.
introCopy: Sweet, savory, and numbing all at once. Toast the peanuts separately for the best crunch.

steps.text: Marinate chicken briefly in soy sauce and a little cornstarch.
Stir-fry dried chilies in oil until fragrant and dark.
Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked through.
Add vinegar, scallions, and peanuts, tossing to combine.
Serve over steamed white rice.

title: Beef and Broccoli
shortDescription: Flank steak, broccoli, garlic, tamari, oyster sauce
note: Slice the beef against the grain and freeze it for 15 minutes first — makes paper-thin slices much easier.
introCopy: Faster than delivery once the beef is sliced, and a lot less salty.

steps.text: Blanch broccoli briefly, then shock in cold water.
Sear beef in a hot wok in batches, then set aside.
Stir-fry garlic briefly, then add broccoli and sauces.
Return beef to the wok and toss to coat.
Serve over steamed white rice.

title: Ratatouille
shortDescription: Eggplant, zucchini, tomato, bell pepper, herbes de provence
note: Cook each vegetable separately before combining — it's slower, but it's the only way to keep them from turning to mush.
introCopy: A slow Sunday project that rewards patience. Just as good, maybe better, the next day.

steps.text: Sauté eggplant separately in olive oil until golden, then set aside.
Repeat with zucchini, then with bell peppers, setting each aside separately.
Sauté onion until soft, then add tomatoes and herbes de provence, simmering into a sauce.
Fold all the vegetables back into the tomato sauce and simmer gently to marry the flavors.

title: Coq au Vin
shortDescription: Chicken thighs, red wine, bacon, mushroom, pearl onion
note: Use a wine you'd actually drink — it reduces down to nearly a third of its volume, so any flaws concentrate too.
introCopy: A weekend project, not a weeknight one. The braise does most of the work once it's in the oven.

ingredients.prepNote: for thickening, use cornstarch for gluten-free

steps.text: Render bacon in a Dutch oven, then brown chicken in the fat and set both aside.
Sauté pearl onions and mushrooms until browned.
Stir in flour, then add wine, scraping up browned bits.
Return chicken and bacon to the pot and braise, covered, in a 325°F oven.
Uncover and reduce the sauce on the stovetop until it coats a spoon.

title: Salade Niçoise
shortDescription: Seared tuna, green beans, egg, olives, potato
note: Sear the tuna hard and fast — a rare center is traditional and it dries out quickly past that point.
introCopy: A composed salad, not a tossed one — each ingredient gets its own spot on the plate.

steps.text: Boil potatoes until tender, then set aside to cool slightly.
Blanch green beans until bright and just tender.
Sear tuna very hot, about 90 seconds per side for a rare center.
Slice tuna and arrange everything on a platter with olives and soft-boiled eggs.

imageCredit: cyclonebill from Copenhagen, Denmark / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Bibimbap
shortDescription: Rice, spinach, carrot, mushroom, fried egg, gochujang
note: Cook each vegetable separately and season individually — that's the difference between bibimbap and a stir-fry over rice.
introCopy: Mix everything together at the table right before eating, not before. Half the appeal is the reveal.

steps.text: Season spinach with sesame oil and a pinch of salt after blanching.
Sauté carrot and mushrooms separately, seasoning each lightly.
Fry eggs sunny-side up with crisp edges.
Arrange rice in bowls topped with each vegetable in its own section, egg on top, gochujang on the side.

imageCredit: Agnes Ly (Agnes Ly) at Flickr / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Korean BBQ Beef Bowl
shortDescription: Ground beef, gochujang, garlic, sesame, rice
note: Cook the beef in batches if the pan looks crowded — steaming instead of browning is the most common way this goes wrong.
introCopy: Sweet-savory ground beef that takes about as long as cooking the rice to go with it.

steps.text: Brown beef in a hot pan in batches so it sears rather than steams.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant.
Stir in tamari, brown sugar, and sesame oil, cooking until glossy.
Serve over rice.

imageCredit: A Healthier Michigan from Detroit, United States / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Kimchi Fried Rice
shortDescription: Day-old rice, kimchi, gochujang, scallion, fried egg
note: Day-old, cold rice is non-negotiable here — fresh warm rice turns to mush the second it hits the pan.
introCopy: The kind of thing to make specifically because the kimchi jar is getting low and sour.

steps.text: Fry kimchi in oil until slightly caramelized at the edges.
Add rice and gochujang, breaking up clumps and tossing to coat.
Fry until the rice picks up some crisp bits at the bottom.
Top each portion with a fried egg and scallions.

title: Margherita Pizza
shortDescription: Pizza dough, San Marzano tomatoes, mozzarella, basil
note: Let the dough come fully to room temperature before stretching — cold dough tears instead of stretching.
introCopy: Three toppings, no more. The whole point is tasting each one, so don't crowd the dough.

steps.text: Preheat oven with a pizza stone or upside-down sheet pan to 500°F for at least 30 minutes.
Stretch dough into a 12-inch round on a floured peel or parchment.
Spread tomatoes thinly, leaving a border, then scatter torn mozzarella.
Slide onto the hot stone and bake until the crust is blistered and cheese bubbles.
Drizzle with olive oil, scatter basil, and slice.

title: Mushroom Risotto
shortDescription: Arborio rice, cremini mushrooms, parmesan, white wine
note: Keep the stock at a bare simmer nearby — cold stock stalls the rice and stretches your cook time.
introCopy: Risotto rewards patience more than skill. Stir often, add stock gradually, and don't walk away.

steps.text: Sauté mushrooms in a splash of oil until browned; set aside.
Cook onion in butter until soft, then stir in rice for a minute until glossy.
Deglaze with wine, then add warm stock a ladle at a time, stirring until absorbed before each addition.
Stir mushrooms back in along with parmesan; season and rest briefly.
Serve immediately while loose and creamy.

title: Chicken Parmesan
shortDescription: Breaded chicken cutlets, marinara, mozzarella, parmesan
note: Pound the cutlets to an even thickness — uneven pieces cook unevenly and dry out at the thin edges.
introCopy: Crisp cutlet, bright sauce, melted cheese. Serve over pasta or on its own with a green salad.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425°F. Dredge cutlets in egg, then breadcrumbs mixed with half the parmesan.
Pan-fry cutlets in oil until golden on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
Transfer to a baking dish, top with marinara, mozzarella, and remaining parmesan.
Bake until cheese is melted and bubbling.
Rest a few minutes before serving.

title: Eggplant Parmesan
shortDescription: Breaded eggplant, marinara, mozzarella, basil
note: Salt the sliced eggplant and let it sit 20 minutes first — it pulls out bitterness and excess moisture.
introCopy: The vegetarian answer to chicken parm, and just as craveable when the eggplant is properly drained first.

steps.text: Rinse and pat dry salted eggplant, then dredge in egg and breadcrumbs.
Bake breaded slices on an oiled sheet at 425°F until golden, flipping once.
Layer eggplant, marinara, and mozzarella in a baking dish, repeating layers.
Top with parmesan and bake until bubbling.
Rest, scatter basil, and serve.

imageCredit: Karen and Brad Emerson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

title: Minestrone Soup
shortDescription: White beans, seasonal vegetables, small pasta, parmesan rind
note: Simmer the parmesan rind in the broth for the last stretch, then fish it out — it adds a savory depth for free.
introCopy: A clean-out-the-fridge soup at heart. Swap in whatever vegetables are around and it still works.

steps.text: Sauté carrots and celery in olive oil until softened.
Add tomatoes, stock, beans, and parmesan rind; bring to a simmer.
Stir in zucchini and pasta, cooking until pasta is tender.
Remove rind, season to taste, and serve with extra parmesan.

imageCredit: Katrin Morenz from Aachen, Deutschland / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Lemon Ricotta Pasta
shortDescription: Pasta, fresh ricotta, lemon zest, parmesan, black pepper
note: Save extra pasta water — the starch is what turns ricotta and lemon into a sauce instead of a topping.
introCopy: Bright, quick, and mostly pantry. Good any night the fridge feels a little empty.

steps.text: Boil pasta in salted water, reserving a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Whisk ricotta, lemon zest and juice, parmesan, and a splash of pasta water into a smooth sauce.
Toss hot pasta with the sauce, loosening with more pasta water as needed.
Finish with cracked pepper and extra parmesan.

imageCredit: Visits to visit / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Chicken Enchiladas Verdes
shortDescription: Shredded chicken, corn tortillas, tomatillo salsa, cotija
note: Warm the tortillas before rolling — cold ones crack instead of folding cleanly.
introCopy: Tangy green salsa instead of red, with a good char under the broiler at the end.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400°F. Warm tortillas until pliable.
Mix chicken with a third of the salsa, then roll into tortillas and arrange in a baking dish.
Pour remaining salsa over the top and scatter both cheeses.
Bake until bubbling, then broil briefly to char the top.
Top with sour cream and cilantro before serving.

title: Shrimp Ceviche
shortDescription: Shrimp, lime juice, tomato, red onion, cilantro, avocado
note: The shrimp needs a genuine 20 minutes in the lime juice to properly firm up and turn opaque — don't rush it.
introCopy: No stove required. Bright, cold, and best eaten the same day with tortilla chips or tostadas.

steps.text: Toss chopped shrimp with lime juice, cover, and refrigerate until opaque and firm.
Drain most of the lime juice, reserving a little for seasoning.
Fold in tomato, onion, jalapeño, and cilantro.
Gently fold in avocado just before serving, season with salt.

imageCredit: No machine-readable author provided. Manuel González Olaechea assumed (based on copyright claims). / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

title: Pork Carnitas
shortDescription: Pork shoulder, orange, garlic, cumin, corn tortillas
note: Resist stirring too often in the last 15 minutes — that's when the edges crisp up in their own fat.
introCopy: Low and slow, then a hot pan at the end for crispy edges. Worth the wait.

steps.text: Season pork with salt, cumin, and oregano, then place in a pot with garlic and orange juice plus halves.
Add water to just cover, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook until fork-tender.
Shred pork and discard orange halves; reduce remaining liquid until syrupy.
Toss shredded pork in the reduced liquid and crisp in a hot skillet in batches.
Serve in warm tortillas with your favorite toppings.

title: Veggie Quesadillas
shortDescription: Flour tortillas, black beans, peppers, corn, cheddar
note: Press the quesadilla flat with a spatula while it cooks so the cheese seals the edges shut.
introCopy: A fast weeknight fallback that's endlessly adaptable to whatever vegetables need using up.

steps.text: Sauté pepper and corn until just softened.
Layer beans, sautéed vegetables, and cheese over half of each tortilla, then fold over.
Cook in a dry skillet until golden and cheese is melted, flipping once.
Slice into wedges and serve with salsa.

imageCredit: brewbooks from near Seattle, USA / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Mexican Street Corn Salad
shortDescription: Grilled corn, cotija, mayo, lime, chili powder, cilantro
note: Char the corn hard before cutting it off the cob — that's most of the flavor in this dish.
introCopy: All the flavor of elote, off the cob, so it's easy to make for a crowd.

steps.text: Grill corn, turning occasionally, until charred in spots.
Cut kernels off the cob into a large bowl.
Toss with mayonnaise, lime juice, half the cotija, and chili powder.
Top with remaining cotija and cilantro before serving.

title: Pozole Rojo
shortDescription: Hominy, pork, dried chiles, cabbage, radish, lime
note: Toast the dried chiles briefly before blending — it wakes up flavor that soaking alone won't reach.
introCopy: A red chile broth built for garnishing generously at the table: cabbage, radish, oregano, lime.

steps.text: Simmer pork in water with garlic until tender, skimming foam.
Toast and soak chiles, then blend with a bit of the pork broth until smooth.
Strain chile mixture into the pot with pork and hominy, and simmer to meld.
Season with salt, ladle into bowls, and serve with cabbage, radish, and lime.

imageCredit: Alejandra Mendoza Santillan / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Teriyaki Chicken Donburi
shortDescription: Chicken thighs, teriyaki glaze, steamed rice, scallion
note: Let the glaze reduce until it coats the back of a spoon — thin glaze just runs off the rice.
introCopy: A rice bowl built around a glossy homemade teriyaki sauce, done faster than delivery.

steps.text: Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until browned, then flip.
Whisk soy sauce, mirin, and sugar, then pour into the pan.
Simmer, spooning sauce over chicken, until glossy and chicken is cooked through.
Slice chicken, serve over rice with sauce spooned on top, scattered with scallion.

title: Pork Gyoza
shortDescription: Ground pork, cabbage, garlic, ginger, dumpling wrappers
note: Don't overfill the wrappers — too much filling makes them impossible to seal and prone to bursting.
introCopy: Crisp on the bottom, tender on top, dipped in a simple soy-vinegar sauce.

steps.text: Mix pork, drained cabbage, garlic, ginger, and soy sauce until combined.
Fill and pleat wrappers with a spoonful of filling each.
Fry dumplings flat-side down in oil until golden on the bottom.
Add a splash of water, cover, and steam until filling is cooked through.
Uncover to crisp the bottoms again before serving with dipping sauce.

title: Salmon Onigiri
shortDescription: Rice, flaked salmon, nori, sesame seeds, salt
note: Wet your hands before shaping each ball — dry hands make the rice stick to you instead of itself.
introCopy: A portable rice ball built around savory flaked salmon, good for lunchboxes or a light snack.

steps.text: Bake or pan-sear salmon until cooked through, then flake into small pieces.
Mix flaked salmon with a pinch of salt and sesame seeds.
With wet hands, shape a portion of rice around a spoonful of salmon into a triangle or ball.
Wrap with a strip of nori and serve at room temperature.

title: Beef Sukiyaki
shortDescription: Thinly sliced beef, tofu, napa cabbage, mushrooms, sukiyaki sauce
note: Slice the beef paper-thin, or ask your butcher to — it should cook in seconds once it hits the pan.
introCopy: A simmered hot-pot style dish, sweet-savory sauce and all, best cooked at the table if you can.

steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, sugar, and mirin with a splash of water for the sukiyaki sauce.
Sear beef slices briefly in a wide pan or hot pot, then push to one side.
Add cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu, then pour in the sauce.
Simmer until vegetables are tender, adding more sauce as it reduces.
Serve straight from the pot over rice.

title: Tofu Katsu Curry
shortDescription: Breaded tofu cutlets, Japanese curry sauce, steamed rice
note: Press the tofu well beforehand — a dry surface is what lets the breading actually stick and crisp.
introCopy: A vegetarian spin on katsu curry: crisp breaded tofu over rice, blanketed in a mellow curry sauce.

steps.text: Simmer onion and carrot in water until tender, then stir in curry roux until dissolved and thickened.
Dredge tofu cutlets in flour, then a beaten-egg wash substitute (water works), then panko.
Pan-fry cutlets until deeply golden on both sides.
Slice cutlets and serve over rice, ladled generously with curry sauce.

imageCredit: Alpha from Melbourne, Australia / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Cold Soba Noodles
shortDescription: Buckwheat soba, dashi dipping sauce, scallion, nori, wasabi
note: Rinse the cooked noodles under cold water and rub gently — it washes off surface starch that would otherwise make them gummy.
introCopy: A refreshing, minimal-effort noodle dish built for a hot day, dipped rather than sauced.

steps.text: Boil soba until just tender, then rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Combine dashi, soy sauce, and mirin, then chill briefly.
Pile noodles onto plates topped with scallion and nori.
Serve with the dipping sauce and wasabi on the side.

imageCredit: Andreas F. Borchert / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
shortDescription: Marinated chicken, tomato cream sauce, garam masala, rice
note: Char the marinated chicken hard under the broiler before it goes into the sauce — that smoky edge is the whole point.
introCopy: Yogurt-marinated chicken finished in a rich tomato sauce. Best made a day ahead so the sauce deepens.

steps.text: Marinate chicken in yogurt and half the garam masala at least 30 minutes.
Broil marinated chicken until charred at the edges.
Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until soft, then add remaining garam masala and tomatoes.
Simmer sauce until thickened, stir in cream, then add chicken and simmer to finish.
Serve over rice with naan.

title: Vegetable Biryani
shortDescription: Basmati rice, mixed vegetables, saffron, whole spices, fried onion
note: Soak the rice for 30 minutes before cooking — it's what gives biryani its long, separate grains.
introCopy: Layered rice and spiced vegetables steamed together until the whole pot smells like saffron and fried onion.

steps.text: Parboil soaked rice with whole spices until three-quarters cooked, then drain.
Cook vegetables with yogurt and biryani spice until just tender.
Layer rice and vegetable mixture in a heavy pot, topping with saffron milk and fried onion.
Cover tightly and steam on low heat until rice is fully cooked and fragrant.
Gently fluff and serve with raita.

title: Dal Tadka
shortDescription: Yellow lentils, cumin, garlic, tomato, tempered ghee
note: Make the tempered oil right before serving and pour it in sizzling — that final crackle is what makes tadka dal taste finished.
introCopy: Simple lentils, elevated entirely by a hot tempering of spices poured over the top at the end.

steps.text: Simmer lentils with turmeric and water until soft and creamy.
Stir in diced tomato and cook a few more minutes.
Heat ghee in a small pan, sizzle cumin, garlic, and chile until fragrant.
Pour the hot tempering over the dal and stir just before serving.
Serve hot over steamed basmati rice.

title: Tandoori Chicken
shortDescription: Chicken, yogurt marinade, tandoori spice, lemon
note: A very hot oven or grill is essential here — tandoori chicken depends on quick, high-heat char, not slow roasting.
introCopy: Deeply spiced and marinated overnight if you can manage it, then blasted at high heat for char.

steps.text: Combine yogurt, tandoori spice, lemon juice, garlic, and ginger, then coat chicken.
Marinate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Roast or grill at high heat, turning once, until charred and cooked through.
Rest briefly, then serve with lemon wedges.

title: Aloo Gobi
shortDescription: Potatoes, cauliflower, turmeric, cumin, ginger
note: Cut potato and cauliflower into similar-sized pieces so they finish cooking at the same time.
introCopy: A dry-spiced vegetable dish, quick enough for a weeknight and equally good as a side.

steps.text: Heat oil, sizzle cumin seeds, then add ginger and turmeric.
Add potatoes and cauliflower, tossing to coat in spices.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until tender.
Season with salt, scatter cilantro, and serve.

imageCredit: Wikimedia Commons contributor / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Rajma Masala
shortDescription: Kidney beans, tomato, onion, garam masala, rice
note: Mash a few beans against the side of the pot near the end — it thickens the gravy without any extra effort.
introCopy: A North Indian kidney bean curry, hearty and simple, classically paired with steamed rice.

steps.text: Sauté onion and garlic until golden.
Stir in garam masala and tomatoes, simmering until thickened.
Add beans and a splash of water, simmering to meld flavors, mashing a few beans.
Serve hot over rice.

title: Pad Thai
shortDescription: Rice noodles, shrimp, egg, tamarind, peanuts, bean sprouts
note: Soak the noodles, don't boil them — boiled rice noodles turn mushy the second they hit the hot pan.
introCopy: Sweet, sour, and salty in careful balance. Have everything prepped before the wok gets hot.

steps.text: Whisk tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar into a sauce.
Stir-fry shrimp until pink, push aside, then scramble egg in the same pan.
Add soaked noodles and sauce, tossing until noodles are tender and coated.
Fold in bean sprouts, then plate and top with crushed peanuts.

title: Massaman Beef Curry
shortDescription: Beef chuck, massaman paste, coconut milk, potato, peanuts
note: Simmer low and slow — the beef needs real time to turn tender, so don't rush it with high heat.
introCopy: A milder, richer Thai curry with Persian-influenced spicing, built for a long weekend simmer.

steps.text: Fry curry paste in a spoonful of coconut cream until fragrant.
Add beef, searing briefly, then pour in remaining coconut milk.
Simmer covered until beef is nearly tender.
Add potatoes, onion, and fish sauce, simmering until everything is tender.
Stir in peanuts and serve with rice.

title: Thai Basil Chicken
shortDescription: Ground chicken, Thai basil, chiles, garlic, fish sauce, fried egg
note: Cook this fast and hot — pad krapow is meant to move quickly in the pan, not simmer.
introCopy: Pad krapow gai: sharp, spicy, and traditionally topped with a crisp fried egg over rice.

steps.text: Fry garlic and chiles in oil over high heat until fragrant.
Add ground chicken, breaking it up, and cook through.
Stir in fish sauce and soy sauce, then basil, wilting it in off heat.
Fry eggs sunny-side up separately, crisping the edges.
Serve chicken over rice topped with a fried egg.

title: Mango Sticky Rice
shortDescription: Glutinous rice, coconut milk, ripe mango, sesame seeds
note: Steam the rice, don't boil it — glutinous rice needs gentle steam heat to turn properly sticky, not gluey.
introCopy: A classic Thai dessert-turned-snack: warm coconut rice next to cool, ripe mango.

steps.text: Steam soaked rice over simmering water until tender and translucent.
Warm coconut milk with sugar and salt until dissolved, reserving some for topping.
Stir most of the coconut mixture into the hot rice and let it absorb.
Serve rice with sliced mango, drizzled with reserved coconut milk and sesame seeds.

imageCredit: Dennis Wong from Hong Kong, Hong Kong / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

title: Som Tum Papaya Salad
shortDescription: Shredded green papaya, lime, chile, fish sauce, peanuts, tomato
note: Bruise the ingredients with a mortar and pestle rather than just tossing them — that's what actually releases the flavor.
introCopy: Sharp, spicy, and no cooking involved. Adjust the chile to taste — it's meant to have real heat.

steps.text: Pound garlic and chiles in a mortar until broken down.
Add tomatoes, lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar, bruising lightly.
Add shredded papaya and peanuts, pounding and tossing to combine.
Taste and adjust lime, sugar, or fish sauce, then serve immediately.

title: Panang Curry Chicken
shortDescription: Chicken, panang curry paste, coconut milk, kaffir lime, peanuts
note: Fry the curry paste in the thick coconut cream that rises to the top of the can — it blooms the spices far better than a thin liquid would.
introCopy: Thicker and nuttier than red curry, with a distinct sweetness balanced by kaffir lime.

steps.text: Fry curry paste in the thick top layer of coconut milk until fragrant.
Add chicken, stirring to coat, then cook until mostly opaque.
Pour in remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, and sugar, simmering until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in kaffir lime leaves and peanuts, then serve over rice.

imageCredit: Alpha from Melbourne, Australia / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: Chicken Shawarma Bowl
shortDescription: Spiced chicken thighs, rice, pickled turnip, garlic sauce
note: Marinate the chicken as long as you can spare — even 30 minutes helps, but a few hours transforms it.
introCopy: Warmly spiced chicken over rice, finished with a garlicky white sauce and something pickled for crunch.

steps.text: Toss chicken with shawarma spice and olive oil, marinating if time allows.
Sear chicken until deeply browned and cooked through, then slice.
Whisk yogurt with garlic and a pinch of salt for the sauce.
Build bowls with rice, sliced chicken, pickled turnip, and garlic sauce.

title: Hummus & Veggie Mezze
shortDescription: Hummus, cucumber, tomato, olives, pita, za'atar
note: A food processor run of at least 3 minutes is what gets hummus truly smooth — don't stop early.
introCopy: A no-cook spread board built around fresh vegetables, olives, and warm pita.

steps.text: Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and a splash of water until very smooth.
Season hummus with salt and spread onto a plate.
Arrange cucumber, tomato, and olives around the hummus.
Sprinkle with za'atar and olive oil, serve with warm pita.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
shortDescription: Chicken, apricots, olives, preserved lemon, warm spices
note: Keep the lid on for most of the cook — the whole point of a tagine is trapping steam so nothing dries out.
introCopy: Sweet and savory in one pot, built on a base of cinnamon, ginger, and turmeric.

steps.text: Brown chicken thighs on both sides, then remove.
Soften onion in the same pot, then stir in spices until fragrant.
Return chicken, add apricots, olives, preserved lemon, and enough water to partly cover.
Cover and simmer until chicken is very tender.
Serve over couscous or rice.

title: Tabbouleh Salad
shortDescription: Bulgur, parsley, mint, tomato, lemon, olive oil
note: Use far more parsley than bulgur by volume — real tabbouleh is a herb salad with a little grain, not the reverse.
introCopy: Bright and herb-forward, best made a little ahead so the lemon and oil can settle in.

steps.text: Soak bulgur in warm water until tender, then drain well.
Combine parsley, mint, tomato, and scallion in a large bowl.
Fold in bulgur, then dress with lemon juice, olive oil, and salt.
Rest 10 minutes before serving so flavors meld.

title: Beef Kebabs with Rice
shortDescription: Ground beef skewers, sumac onions, warm spices, rice
note: Chill the shaped kebabs for 15 minutes before grilling — it helps them hold together on the skewer.
introCopy: Simple spiced beef skewers, best cooked over high heat until charred at the edges.

steps.text: Mix beef with grated onion, cumin, paprika, and salt.
Shape around skewers into long kebabs, chilling briefly.
Grill, turning occasionally, until charred and cooked through.
Toss sliced red onion with sumac and a pinch of salt.
Serve kebabs over rice topped with sumac onions.

title: Fattoush Salad
shortDescription: Mixed greens, radish, tomato, cucumber, crispy pita, sumac
note: Toss the fried or toasted pita in right before serving — dressed too early and it goes soggy fast.
introCopy: A crunchy, tangy salad that turns leftover pita into the best part of the dish.

steps.text: Toast torn pita pieces until crisp, in the oven or a dry skillet.
Toss greens, cucumber, radish, and tomato in a large bowl.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, and sumac, then dress the salad.
Scatter crispy pita on top just before serving.

imageCredit: Wikimedia Commons contributor / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

title: BBQ Pulled Pork Sandwich
shortDescription: Pork shoulder, BBQ sauce, coleslaw, brioche bun
note: Let the pork rest 15 minutes before shredding — it reabsorbs juice instead of losing it all to the cutting board.
introCopy: Slow-cooked pork shredded into sauce, piled onto a bun with slaw for crunch.

steps.text: Season pork and slow-cook with half the BBQ sauce until fall-apart tender.
Shred pork, discard excess fat, and toss with remaining sauce.
Toss coleslaw mix with mayonnaise and a pinch of salt.
Pile pork onto buns and top with coleslaw.

imageCredit: Infrogmation of New Orleans / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Mac and Cheese
shortDescription: Elbow pasta, cheddar, gruyere, butter, milk
note: Take the roux off heat before whisking in cheese — too hot and the cheese turns grainy instead of silky.
introCopy: A stovetop cheese sauce, no baking required, ready faster than the boxed version.

steps.text: Boil macaroni until al dente, drain.
Melt butter, whisk in flour, and cook a minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk, cooking until thickened.
Off heat, whisk in cheeses until smooth, then fold in pasta.
Season and serve immediately.

title: Cobb Salad
shortDescription: Chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, blue cheese, tomato, greens
note: Keep each ingredient in its own neat row rather than tossing — that's what makes a Cobb a Cobb.
introCopy: A composed salad with enough protein to be a full meal, no single bite quite like the last.

steps.text: Arrange romaine on a platter as the base.
Line up chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, blue cheese, and tomato in rows across the top.
Drizzle with vinaigrette just before serving, or serve on the side.

imageCredit: Ser Amantio di Nicolao / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Grilled Chicken Caesar Salad
shortDescription: Grilled chicken, romaine, parmesan, croutons, Caesar dressing
note: Let grilled chicken rest 5 minutes before slicing so the juices stay in the meat, not on the cutting board.
introCopy: A weeknight staple: grilled chicken over crisp romaine with a punchy, garlicky dressing.

steps.text: Season chicken and grill until cooked through, then rest and slice.
Toss romaine with Caesar dressing and most of the parmesan.
Top with sliced chicken, croutons, and remaining parmesan.

imageCredit: Prayitno / Thank you for (12 millions +) view from Los Angeles, USA / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

title: Loaded Baked Potato Soup
shortDescription: Potatoes, bacon, cheddar, sour cream, chives
note: Mash some of the potatoes right in the pot near the end — it thickens the soup without needing extra cream.
introCopy: Everything you'd pile onto a baked potato, blended into a soup instead.

steps.text: Simmer potatoes in stock until very tender.
Mash about half the potatoes right in the pot for texture.
Stir in cheddar and sour cream until melted and smooth.
Ladle into bowls and top with bacon and chives.

title: Buffalo Cauliflower Bites
shortDescription: Cauliflower florets, buffalo sauce, blue cheese dip, celery
note: Bake at high heat and don't crowd the pan — steamed cauliflower won't crisp, no matter the sauce.
introCopy: A vegetarian take on a bar snack: roasted cauliflower tossed hot in buffalo sauce.

steps.text: Toss cauliflower florets with olive oil and roast at 425°F until browned.
Toss hot cauliflower with buffalo sauce.
Return to the oven briefly to set the sauce.
Serve with blue cheese dressing and celery.

imageCredit: Tony Webster from Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

title: Vegetable Fried Rice
shortDescription: Day-old rice, egg, carrot, peas, scallion, soy sauce
note: Use rice that's been refrigerated overnight — fresh rice is too moist and turns the whole pan mushy.
introCopy: The best use for leftover rice, done in one hot pan in under 20 minutes.

steps.text: Scramble egg in hot oil until just set, then remove.
Stir-fry carrot and peas until crisp-tender.
Add rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry until heated through and slightly crisp.
Return egg, add soy sauce and scallion, tossing to combine.

imageCredit: Ganesh Mohan T / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Sweet and Sour Chicken
shortDescription: Battered chicken, pineapple, bell pepper, sweet-sour sauce
note: Fry in two batches if needed — an overcrowded pan steams the batter instead of crisping it.
introCopy: A takeout favorite made at home, with a tangy sauce that's easy to dial up or down.

steps.text: Toss chicken in cornstarch and fry until golden and cooked through.
Stir-fry bell pepper and pineapple briefly.
Whisk vinegar, sugar, and ketchup, then pour into the pan and simmer until glossy.
Return chicken, tossing to coat in sauce, then serve over rice.

title: Dan Dan Noodles
shortDescription: Wheat noodles, ground pork, chili oil, sesame paste, scallion
note: Build the sauce in the bowl first, then add hot noodles on top — that's what melts everything together properly.
introCopy: Spicy, nutty, and quick — a Sichuan noodle dish that comes together almost entirely at the last minute.

steps.text: Boil noodles until just tender.
Brown ground pork in a hot pan until crisp in spots.
Whisk chili oil, sesame paste, and soy sauce in each serving bowl.
Top with noodles, pork, and scallion, tossing at the table before eating.

imageCredit: Steven G. Johnson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

title: Chicken Chow Mein
shortDescription: Egg noodles, chicken, cabbage, carrot, soy sauce
note: Cook the noodles slightly under, since they'll finish softening in the stir-fry itself.
introCopy: A fast noodle stir-fry that's endlessly forgiving with whatever vegetables are in the fridge.

steps.text: Boil noodles until just tender, then drain and rinse briefly.
Stir-fry chicken until cooked through, then remove.
Stir-fry cabbage and carrot until just softened.
Add noodles, chicken, soy sauce, and oyster sauce, tossing until combined and hot.

imageCredit: Gaurav Dhwaj Khadka / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Hot and Sour Soup
shortDescription: Tofu, mushrooms, bamboo shoots, egg, vinegar, white pepper
note: Drizzle the beaten egg in slowly while stirring the soup gently — that's what creates the classic ribbons.
introCopy: Tangy, peppery, and quick to make once the ingredients are prepped.

steps.text: Simmer stock with mushrooms and bamboo shoots.
Add tofu, vinegar, and white pepper, simmering a few more minutes.
Drizzle in beaten egg while stirring gently to form ribbons.
Season to taste and serve hot.

title: Sichuan Green Beans
shortDescription: Green beans, ground pork, garlic, chili, Sichuan peppercorn
note: Blister the beans hard before adding anything else — that dry-fried char is what makes this dish work.
introCopy: Dry-fried until wrinkled and blistered, then tossed with a little spiced pork for depth.

steps.text: Dry-fry green beans in a hot, lightly oiled pan until blistered and wrinkled.
Remove beans, then brown ground pork with garlic, chiles, and peppercorn.
Return beans, add soy sauce, and toss to combine.

imageCredit: Ewan Munro from London, UK / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

title: French Onion Soup
shortDescription: Caramelized onions, beef stock, gruyere, baguette
note: Give the onions real time — 45 minutes of low, patient cooking is what turns them deeply sweet, not just soft.
introCopy: Slow caramelized onions in a rich broth, finished under the broiler with melted gruyere.

steps.text: Cook onions in butter over low heat, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized.
Deglaze with wine, then add stock and simmer.
Ladle into oven-safe bowls, top with toasted baguette and gruyere.
Broil until cheese is melted and bubbling.

title: Quiche Lorraine
shortDescription: Pie crust, bacon, eggs, cream, gruyere
note: Blind-bake the crust first — skip this and the bottom stays raw under the custard.
introCopy: A classic savory custard tart, just as good warm from the oven or cold the next day.

steps.text: Blind-bake the pie crust until just set, about 10 minutes at 375°F.
Scatter bacon and gruyere over the crust.
Whisk eggs, cream, nutmeg, and a pinch of salt, then pour over.
Bake until just set in the center with a slight jiggle.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Beef Bourguignon
shortDescription: Beef chuck, red wine, mushrooms, pearl onions, bacon
note: Sear the beef in batches — crowd the pan and it steams instead of browning, which is most of the dish's flavor.
introCopy: A long, slow braise in red wine. Worth doing on a weekend when you're around the house anyway.

steps.text: Render bacon, then sear beef in batches in the rendered fat until browned.
Stir in tomato paste, then deglaze with wine and add stock.
Cover and braise until beef is very tender.
Stir in mushrooms and pearl onions, simmering uncovered until sauce thickens.
Serve with crusty bread or mashed potatoes.

title: Croque Monsieur
shortDescription: Ham, gruyere, béchamel, sourdough bread
note: Spread béchamel on the outside of the sandwich too — that's what crisps into a golden crust in the oven.
introCopy: A grilled ham and cheese sandwich elevated with a rich béchamel and a broiled cheese top.

steps.text: Melt butter, whisk in flour, then gradually whisk in milk to make a thick béchamel.
Assemble sandwiches with ham and half the gruyere.
Spread béchamel over the tops, then scatter remaining gruyere.
Bake or broil until golden and bubbling.

title: Chicken Provençal
shortDescription: Chicken thighs, tomatoes, olives, herbes de Provence, white wine
note: Nestle the chicken skin-side up after searing so it stays crisp instead of steaming in the sauce.
introCopy: A rustic braise leaning on tomatoes, olives, and dried herbs rather than heavy cream.

steps.text: Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden, then remove.
Soften garlic in the same pan, then deglaze with wine.
Add tomatoes, olives, and herbs, then nestle chicken back in skin-side up.
Simmer covered until chicken is cooked through and tender.
Serve with crusty bread or rice.

title: Leek and Potato Soup
shortDescription: Leeks, potatoes, stock, cream, chives
note: Rinse the sliced leeks thoroughly — grit hides between the layers and no one wants it in the finished soup.
introCopy: Silky and simple, delicious hot or chilled as vichyssoise on a warm day.

steps.text: Soften leeks in butter without browning.
Add potatoes and stock, simmering until potatoes are very tender.
Blend until smooth, then stir in cream.
Serve hot, or chill fully for cold vichyssoise, topped with chives.

title: Korean Fried Chicken
shortDescription: Double-fried chicken wings, gochujang glaze, sesame
note: Fry twice — the first fry cooks the meat, the second makes the skin shatter-crisp.
introCopy: Double-frying is the whole trick here: it renders out extra fat so the skin stays crisp even under a sticky glaze.

steps.text: Toss wings in potato starch, shaking off excess.
Fry wings at 325°F until pale gold, then rest 10 minutes.
Fry again at 375°F until deeply golden and crackling-crisp.
Whisk gochujang, honey, and garlic in a pan and warm until glossy.
Toss fried wings in the glaze and finish with sesame seeds.

title: Japchae Noodles
shortDescription: Sweet potato glass noodles, vegetables, beef, sesame oil
note: Cook and season each vegetable separately before combining — it keeps every ingredient's texture distinct.
introCopy: A stir-fried noodle dish where the glass noodles stay chewy and slightly sweet, studded with quick-cooked vegetables.

steps.text: Boil noodles until tender, rinse, and cut into shorter lengths.
Blanch spinach briefly and squeeze dry; season lightly.
Stir-fry beef until browned; set aside.
Stir-fry carrot, onion, and mushrooms separately until just tender.
Toss noodles with soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar, then fold in everything else.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
shortDescription: Aged kimchi, pork belly, tofu, gochugaru broth
note: Use kimchi that's past its prime and well-fermented — sour, funky kimchi makes a far deeper broth than fresh.
introCopy: A bubbling stew built on aged kimchi's sourness, rounded out with pork and soft tofu.

steps.text: Render pork belly in the pot until lightly browned.
Add kimchi and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add gochugaru, gochujang, and water; bring to a boil.
Simmer until pork is tender and broth deepens in color.
Add tofu and simmer gently, then top with scallion.
Serve hot with steamed short-grain rice.

title: Bulgogi Lettuce Wraps
shortDescription: Marinated beef, butter lettuce, ssamjang, rice
note: Slice the beef thin and against the grain — it's what lets a quick marinade fully penetrate in under an hour.
introCopy: Sweet-savory marinated beef, wrapped fresh in lettuce with a dab of spicy ssamjang.

steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, grated pear, and garlic.
Marinate beef at least 30 minutes.
Sear beef over high heat in batches until charred at the edges.
Serve beef in lettuce leaves with a dab of ssamjang and rice on the side.

title: Sundubu Jjigae
shortDescription: Soft silken tofu, gochugaru broth, egg, scallion
note: Keep the tofu whole and spoon it apart in the pot — cubing it beforehand breaks it down to mush.
introCopy: A fiery, custard-soft tofu stew served bubbling in its own stone pot, finished with a cracked egg.

steps.text: Bloom gochugaru in sesame oil with garlic until fragrant.
Add broth and bring to a boil.
Spoon tofu into the pot in large curds and simmer.
Crack an egg into each portion and simmer until just set, then top with scallion.

title: Gochujang-Glazed Salmon
shortDescription: Salmon fillets, gochujang, honey, garlic, sesame
note: Broil at the very end just to lacquer the glaze — any longer and the sugar in it will scorch.
introCopy: A sheet-pan salmon dinner with a sweet-spicy glaze that caramelizes under the broiler in minutes.

steps.text: Whisk gochujang, honey, soy sauce, garlic, and sesame oil.
Brush salmon generously with the glaze on a lined sheet pan.
Bake until nearly cooked through.
Broil briefly to caramelize the glaze, then scatter with sesame seeds.

title: Chicken Adobo
shortDescription: Chicken thighs, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaf
note: Don't stir the vinegar in too early — let it simmer uncovered a few minutes first so the sharpness mellows.
introCopy: The Philippines' everyday braise: chicken simmered in soy sauce and vinegar until the sauce turns dark and clingy.

steps.text: Combine chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot; marinate 15 minutes.
Bring to a boil uncovered, then simmer uncovered until vinegar's sharpness mellows.
Cover and simmer until chicken is tender.
Uncover and reduce sauce until thickened and glossy. Serve over rice.

imageCredit: dbgg1979 on flickr / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

title: Pork Sinigang
shortDescription: Pork ribs, tamarind broth, radish, spinach, green beans
note: Add leafy greens only in the last minute — sinigang greens should stay bright, not stewed to gray.
introCopy: A sour tamarind soup built for grey, rainy days, loaded with pork and whatever vegetables are on hand.

steps.text: Simmer pork ribs with onion and tomato in water until tender.
Stir in tamarind base and radish; simmer until radish softens.
Add green beans and simmer briefly.
Stir in spinach just until wilted, then serve hot with rice.

imageCredit: Ralff Nestor Nacor / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

title: Pancit Bihon
shortDescription: Rice noodles, chicken, cabbage, carrot, soy sauce
note: Soak the rice noodles, don't boil them — boiling turns them to mush before they even hit the pan.
introCopy: A stir-fried rice noodle dish served at every Filipino birthday for long life — thin noodles, quick vegetables, fast weeknight food.

steps.text: Sauté garlic, then chicken until cooked through.
Add cabbage and carrot; stir-fry until just tender.
Pour in broth and soy sauce, bring to a simmer.
Add soaked noodles and toss until they absorb the liquid and soften.

title: Filipino Lumpia
shortDescription: Ground pork, carrot, onion, spring roll wrappers, fried
note: Roll tightly and seal the edge with a dab of water — loose rolls burst open in the fryer.
introCopy: Crisp, thin-wrapped fried spring rolls packed with seasoned ground pork, a party-table staple.

steps.text: Mix pork, carrot, onion, garlic, and salt until well combined.
Roll filling tightly into wrappers, sealing edges with water.
Fry in batches until deeply golden and crisp.
Drain on a rack and serve with a vinegar dipping sauce.

title: Chicken Pho
shortDescription: Chicken broth, rice noodles, star anise, herbs, lime
note: Char the onion and ginger before simmering — it's what gives the broth its signature smoky depth.
introCopy: A fragrant, long-simmered chicken broth over silky rice noodles, finished at the table with fresh herbs and lime.

steps.text: Simmer chicken bones and thighs, skimming impurities, until broth is clear.
Add charred onion, ginger, and spices; simmer low and slow.
Strain broth and season with fish sauce and salt.
Cook rice noodles, ladle broth over, top with shredded chicken and herbs.

title: Banh Mi Sandwich
shortDescription: Baguette, pork, pickled carrot and daikon, cilantro, pate
note: Pickle the vegetables at least an hour ahead — a rushed quick-pickle stays too raw and crunchy-sharp.
introCopy: A crackly baguette stacked with savory pork, tangy pickles, and fresh herbs — French bread, Vietnamese soul.

steps.text: Pickle carrot and daikon in vinegar, sugar, and salt at least an hour ahead.
Sear marinated pork until caramelized at the edges.
Split and lightly toast baguettes; spread with mayonnaise.
Layer pork, pickled vegetables, cilantro, and jalapeño.

title: Vietnamese Spring Rolls
shortDescription: Rice paper, shrimp, vermicelli, herbs, peanut sauce
note: Dip the rice paper only briefly — it keeps softening after you pull it out, so slightly firm is exactly right.
introCopy: Fresh, uncooked rolls wrapped in translucent rice paper, dunked in a rich peanut dipping sauce.

steps.text: Cook vermicelli and shrimp; prep all vegetables and herbs.
Dip rice paper briefly in warm water until just pliable.
Layer shrimp, noodles, lettuce, carrot, and herbs, then roll tightly.
Whisk peanut butter dipping sauce and serve alongside.

title: Vietnamese Caramel Pork
shortDescription: Pork belly, caramel sauce, fish sauce, coconut water, egg
note: Cook the sugar to a deep amber before adding pork — pale caramel gives a flat, one-note sweetness.
introCopy: Thit kho — pork belly braised low and slow in a bittersweet caramel sauce until deeply savory and tender.

steps.text: Melt sugar in a pot until deep amber caramel forms.
Add pork belly and toss to coat in caramel, then add garlic and fish sauce.
Pour in coconut water and simmer, partially covered, until pork is tender.
Add hard-boiled eggs, simmer to absorb sauce, and top with scallion.

title: Greek Chicken Souvlaki
shortDescription: Skewered chicken, lemon, oregano, garlic, pita, tzatziki
note: Cut chicken into evenly sized cubes — mismatched pieces mean some skewers dry out before others finish.
introCopy: Bright, lemony grilled skewers wrapped in warm pita with cool, garlicky tzatziki.

steps.text: Marinate chicken in olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, and garlic.
Thread chicken onto skewers.
Grill, turning occasionally, until charred and cooked through.
Warm pita and serve with tzatziki.

title: Greek Salad
shortDescription: Tomato, cucumber, red onion, feta, olives, oregano
note: Salt the tomatoes and cucumber a few minutes ahead and drain — it keeps the salad from turning watery.
introCopy: No lettuce, no fuss — just ripe tomato, cucumber, briny olives, and a thick slab of feta on top.

steps.text: Combine tomato, cucumber, onion, and olives in a bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil and season lightly.
Top with a slab of feta and a scatter of oregano.

title: Spanakopita
shortDescription: Spinach, feta, phyllo dough, dill, egg
note: Squeeze the spinach bone-dry before mixing — excess moisture turns the phyllo layers soggy in the oven.
introCopy: Flaky, buttery phyllo wrapped around a garlicky spinach-and-feta filling — a classic savory Greek pie.

steps.text: Mix spinach, feta, eggs, sautéed onion, and dill.
Layer half the phyllo sheets in a baking dish, brushing each with butter.
Spread filling evenly, then layer remaining phyllo on top, buttering each sheet.
Score the top and bake until golden and crisp.

title: Greek Lemon Orzo Soup
shortDescription: Chicken broth, orzo, egg, lemon, shredded chicken
note: Temper the egg-lemon mixture with hot broth gradually before adding it back — pouring it straight in will scramble the eggs.
introCopy: Avgolemono — a silky, tangy chicken soup thickened with whisked egg and brightened with lemon.

steps.text: Simmer broth and cook orzo until tender.
Whisk eggs and lemon juice together.
Temper the egg mixture with ladles of hot broth, whisking constantly.
Stir tempered mixture back into the pot with shredded chicken; warm gently without boiling.

title: Jollof Rice
shortDescription: Rice, tomato, red pepper, onion, scotch bonnet, spices
note: Blend and reduce the tomato-pepper base until it's thick and deeply concentrated before adding rice — a watery base gives mushy, pale rice.
introCopy: West Africa's iconic one-pot rice, cooked entirely in a smoky, reduced tomato-pepper sauce.

steps.text: Blend tomatoes, bell pepper, half the onion, and scotch bonnet until smooth.
Sauté remaining onion and tomato paste in oil until deep red.
Add blended mixture and simmer, reducing until thick and darkened.
Stir in rice and broth, cover, and cook low until rice is tender and edges are slightly smoky.

title: West African Fufu
shortDescription: Cassava and plantain flour, water, served with soup
note: Stir constantly and vigorously over low heat — fufu needs a strong arm to reach its stretchy, smooth texture.
introCopy: A smooth, stretchy starch staple made by working cassava and plantain flour into a soft dough, meant for scooping soup.

steps.text: Bring water to a boil in a heavy pot.
Whisk in cassava and plantain flour gradually to avoid lumps.
Stir vigorously and constantly over low heat until smooth, stretchy, and no longer grainy.
Shape into rounds with wet hands and serve alongside soup or stew.

title: Peanut Groundnut Stew
shortDescription: Chicken, peanut butter, tomato, onion, ginger, spinach
note: Whisk the peanut butter with warm broth before adding it to the pot — dropping it in whole makes it clump instead of blending smooth.
introCopy: A rich, nutty West African stew where natural peanut butter melts into a deeply savory tomato base.

steps.text: Brown chicken thighs, then set aside.
Sauté onion and ginger, then add crushed tomatoes and simmer.
Whisk peanut butter into warm broth until smooth, then stir into the pot.
Return chicken to the pot and simmer until tender; stir in spinach at the end.
Serve hot over steamed white rice.

title: Suya Skewers
shortDescription: Beef, peanut spice rub, onion, tomato, ground chili
note: Coat the meat in the ground-peanut yaji spice twice — once before grilling, once right after, for the full crust.
introCopy: Nigerian street-food skewers coated in a bold, peanut-based spice rub, char-grilled and sliced onto a plate of onion and tomato.

steps.text: Mix ground peanuts, chili, ginger, and onion powder into a dry spice rub.
Thread beef onto skewers and coat generously with the rub.
Grill over high heat, turning, until charred at the edges.
Dust with more spice rub and serve with sliced onion and tomato.

title: Feijoada
shortDescription: Black beans, pork, sausage, orange, rice
note: Soak the beans overnight and skim the pot often — a clean simmer keeps the stew from turning muddy.
introCopy: Brazil's national dish: a deeply savory black bean and pork stew simmered low and slow, served with rice and orange slices.

steps.text: Sauté onion and garlic, then brown pork shoulder and sausage.
Add soaked beans, bay leaves, and enough water to cover generously.
Simmer, skimming occasionally, until beans and pork are tender.
Uncover and simmer to thicken slightly; serve with rice and orange slices.

title: Brazilian Picanha
shortDescription: Beef sirloin cap, coarse salt, garlic, chimichurri
note: Leave the fat cap on and score it lightly — it's what bastes the meat and crisps up over the fire.
introCopy: A churrasco classic: beef sirloin cap seasoned with nothing but coarse salt and grilled hot for a deeply crusted exterior.

ingredients.prepNote: tomato, onion, bell pepper, red wine vinegar

steps.text: Cut beef into thick steaks along the grain, leaving the fat cap intact.
Season generously with coarse salt just before grilling.
Grill fat-side down first over high heat, then sear all sides to desired doneness.
While the meat rests, warm the rice and black beans, toast the farofa, and stir together the vinagrete.
Rest the meat, slice against the grain, and serve with the rice, beans, farofa, vinagrete, and chimichurri.

title: Brazilian Shrimp Moqueca
shortDescription: Shrimp, coconut milk, tomato, bell pepper, palm oil, cilantro
note: Add the shrimp last and barely simmer them — moqueca's shrimp should stay just-cooked and plump, not rubbery.
introCopy: A vividly orange coconut-milk shrimp stew from Bahia, fragrant with peppers and a touch of palm oil.

steps.text: Sauté onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add tomato and simmer until it breaks down.
Stir in coconut milk and palm oil; simmer to meld flavors.
Add shrimp and simmer just until pink and cooked through, then top with cilantro.

imageCredit: Luca Nebuloni from Milan, Italy / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

title: Pão de Queijo
shortDescription: Tapioca flour, cheese, milk, eggs, oil
note: Blend the batter until completely smooth — lumps of tapioca flour won't puff evenly in the oven.
introCopy: Brazilian cheese bread — naturally gluten-free, chewy in the middle, with a light crackly crust.

steps.text: Heat milk and oil until just simmering, then pour over tapioca flour.
Blend in eggs, cheese, and salt until smooth batter forms.
Fill greased muffin cups two-thirds full.
Bake until puffed and golden.

title: Turkish Lamb Kebabs
shortDescription: Ground lamb, onion, parsley, cumin, sumac, flatbread
note: Chill the shaped kebabs for 20 minutes before grilling — cold meat holds its shape on the skewer instead of slumping off.
introCopy: Adana-style kebabs: spiced ground lamb pressed onto skewers and grilled hot for a deep char.

steps.text: Mix lamb, onion, parsley, cumin, sumac, and aleppo pepper thoroughly.
Shape mixture onto flat skewers, pressing firmly, and chill.
Grill over high heat, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Serve on warm flatbread with extra parsley and sumac.

title: Turkish Lentil Soup
shortDescription: Red lentils, onion, carrot, cumin, mint, lemon
note: Blend the soup until fully smooth — a silky texture is what makes this soup feel comforting rather than rustic.
introCopy: Mercimek çorbası — a velvety red lentil soup finished with a swirl of butter, mint, and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Sauté onion and carrot until softened, then add cumin.
Add lentils and broth; simmer until lentils fall apart.
Blend until smooth, adjusting thickness with water if needed.
Finish with lemon juice and a drizzle of melted butter.

title: Turkish Menemen
shortDescription: Eggs, tomato, green pepper, onion, butter
note: Keep the heat low and stir gently once the eggs go in — menemen should stay soft-scrambled, not fully set.
introCopy: A soft, saucy scrambled-egg dish simmered right into a bed of stewed tomato and green pepper.

steps.text: Sauté onion and green pepper in butter until softened.
Add tomato and simmer until it breaks down into a thick sauce.
Crack in eggs and stir gently over low heat until softly set.
Dust with aleppo pepper and serve with bread.

title: Turkish Pide
shortDescription: Boat-shaped flatbread, ground beef, peppers, cheese
note: Pinch the edges tightly into a boat shape before topping — a loose edge lets the filling spill during baking.
introCopy: A boat-shaped stuffed flatbread, baked hot and fast until the crust blisters and the filling turns savory-rich.

steps.text: Mix ground beef, pepper, tomato, and tomato paste for the filling.
Roll dough into oval shapes and pinch edges into a boat.
Spread filling down the center and top with cheese.
Bake at high heat until crust is blistered and filling cooked through.

title: Chicken Satay
shortDescription: Skewered chicken, peanut sauce, turmeric, coconut milk
note: Marinate at least an hour — the turmeric and coconut milk need time to actually color and tenderize the chicken.
introCopy: Grilled turmeric-marinated chicken skewers served with a thick, spiced peanut dipping sauce.

steps.text: Marinate chicken in turmeric and coconut milk at least an hour.
Thread chicken onto skewers.
Grill, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, brown sugar, and sambal into a sauce for dipping.

title: Nasi Goreng
shortDescription: Fried rice, kecap manis, shallot, chili, fried egg
note: Use rice that's been chilled overnight — fresh warm rice turns gummy and clumps in the wok.
introCopy: Indonesia's smoky-sweet fried rice, colored deep brown by kecap manis and topped with a fried egg.

steps.text: Stir-fry shallot, garlic, and chili until fragrant.
Add rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry until heated through.
Stir in kecap manis until rice is evenly colored.
Top each portion with a fried egg and scallion.

title: Beef Rendang
shortDescription: Beef chuck, coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal, chili paste
note: Let the sauce reduce all the way to a thick, dark paste clinging to the meat — rushed rendang stays a thin curry instead.
introCopy: A slow-cooked, deeply spiced beef dish where coconut milk reduces down into an almost caramelized, clinging sauce.

steps.text: Blend chili, garlic, and aromatics into a paste.
Sauté the paste with lemongrass and galangal until fragrant.
Add beef and coconut milk; bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until sauce reduces to a thick, dark paste.
Serve over steamed white rice.

title: Gado-Gado
shortDescription: Blanched vegetables, tofu, boiled egg, peanut sauce
note: Keep each vegetable's blanching time separate — cramming them all in one pot overcooks the tender ones before the firm ones are done.
introCopy: An Indonesian salad of blanched and raw vegetables, tofu, and egg, all bound together by a rich peanut dressing.

steps.text: Blanch green beans and bean sprouts separately until just tender.
Whisk peanut butter, kecap manis, and warm water into a smooth dressing.
Arrange vegetables, tofu, cucumber, and egg on a platter.
Drizzle generously with peanut dressing just before serving.
